T: The convent choir just got soul. So did the kitchen.
D: A Reno lounge singer hides from the mob in a San Francisco convent and turns the choir around.
P: Serve the mains when Deloris sits down to her first plain convent dinner.
S: the casino lounge where Deloris sings
Button mushroom caps filled with fried bacon, garlic, breadcrumbs and parmesan, then baked until golden on top.
San Francisco, the convent's home city

Creamy clam chowder with bacon, potato and thyme, ladled into hollowed sourdough rolls toasted crisp and topped with crumbled bacon and chives. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp, set half aside. Soften an onion and 2 celery sticks in the fat, stir in 2 tbsp flour, then add 300ml fish stock, 300ml milk and 2 diced potatoes and simmer 15 minutes. Add 2 drained 280g cans of baby clams and 150ml cream and heat through. Hollow 4 small sourdough rolls and toast at 200C for 6 minutes. Fill with chowder and top with bacon and chives.
the choir's tea break after rehearsal
Scones with grated cheddar, chives and a pinch of cayenne, baked at 220C for 12 minutes, butter on the side.
M: the bland convent dinner Deloris can't believe
Beef chuck browned, onion, garlic, smoked paprika, thyme and a splash of hot sauce, stock and tomato, braised 3 hours with potatoes and carrots. Proper flavour this time.
Late night bar cheeseburgers and fries
the nuns sneaking into the bar across the road

Thick chuck patties grilled to medium with melted cheddar, onion, lettuce, pickles and burger sauce on a toasted bun, with crisp double-fried chips. Cut 1kg potatoes into chips, soak 30 minutes, dry and fry at 140C for 6 minutes, then at 190C until crisp. Shape 800g chuck mince into 4 thick patties and season. Grill over high heat for 4 minutes a side, adding a slice of cheddar for the last minute. Mix 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp tomato sauce and 1 tbsp chopped pickles. Build on toasted buns with lettuce, onion and pickles.
W: the sisters never waste a loaf
Buttered bread layered with sultanas in a baked vanilla custard, crisp on top and soft underneath.
K: Choir practice honey ginger lemon tea

Fresh ginger simmered with lemon and cinnamon, steeped with black tea and sweetened with honey, served hot in plain white cups with a lemon slice. Slice a 5cm knob of ginger and simmer in 1.2L water with a cinnamon stick for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat, add 4 black tea bags and steep for 4 minutes, then remove the bags. Stir in the juice of a lemon and 4 tbsp honey. Pour into plain white cups and float a thin lemon slice in each.

s.note: the casino lounge where Deloris sings
s.how: Remove the stems from 20 button mushrooms and chop the stems. Fry with 2 rashers diced bacon and 1 crushed garlic clove, then mix with 1/2 cup breadcrumbs and 50g grated parmesan. Fill the caps and bake at 200C for 15 minutes.

s.note: the choir's tea break after rehearsal
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, then stir in 150g grated vintage cheddar, chopped chives and a pinch of cayenne. Mix in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with butter.

m.note: the bland convent dinner Deloris can't believe
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 onions, crushed garlic, a spoon of smoked paprika and thyme. Pour in stock, a can of tomatoes and a splash of hot sauce. Braise for 3 hours, adding potatoes and carrots for the last hour. Proper flavour this time.

w.note: the sisters never waste a loaf
w.how: Butter 8 slices of white bread, cut into triangles and layer in a dish with 80g sultanas. Whisk 3 eggs, 500ml milk, 100ml cream, 70g sugar and 1 tsp vanilla, pour over and soak 20 minutes. Sprinkle with nutmeg and bake at 170C for 40 minutes until puffed and golden.
